transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Atlas), Jordan Lee (Atlas), Samantha Wu (Atlas)

Summary: Quick alignment on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed on benchmark approach and reporting format (CSV + dashboard snapshot). Agreed timeline: run benchmarks week of Oct 13, aim to close POC in 3-4 weeks subject to results.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, hope you all can hear me ok, um, quick intros?
[00:08] Priya (Atlas): Hi, this is Priya, Head of ML at AtlasHealth. We're focused on inference for clinical triage models.
[00:12] Jordan (Atlas): Jordan here, infra eng, I'll handle network and security stuff.
[00:16] Samantha (Atlas): Samantha, product, watching success criteria and timeline.
[00:22] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hey all, Carlos, I'll lead the benchmark & config side.
[00:25] Lena: Great. The goal today is to sign off success criteria and acceptance tests for the POC, confirm workload sizing, and agree next steps.

[02:05] Priya: To be concrete, our production layer expects P95 latency under 300ms for 512-token gen, throughput ~50 qps for peak windows, and cost target around $0.0009 per token equivalent — those are ballpark. Also data residency in US-EAST for PHI reasons.
[02:30] Jordan: We'll need SOC2 attestation and KMS integration; SSO via SAML is required for engineers.
[02:45] Carlos: Noted. From Redwood side we can run on hosted or dedicated; for this POC we'd propose Redwood Dedicated in US-EAST to hit throughput targets and isolate data, but we can also run a hosted test if you prefer faster kickoff.
[03:20] Priya: For the POC we prefer private/dedicated-ish isolation, but if hosted can do VPC peering and KMS, that's acceptable. The decision depends on perf.

[05:10] Lena: Ok let's focus on measurable success criteria. Proposed acceptance tests:
 - Latency: P95 <= 300ms for 512 tokens (go threshold), P95 <= 350ms (soft threshold / warning).
 - Throughput: sustain 50 qps with 95% load average for a 30 min soak.
 - Accuracy/regression: end-to-end outputs must match baseline within acceptable drift; we'll use a 500-sample prompt set and expect no >5% quality regressions on targeted metrics (precision/recall of entity extraction).
 - Cost: per-token cost improvement target vs current baseline (they had a prior cloud run) — aim for <= 1.2x current spend per request.
 - Security: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration validated (checklist).

[07:00] Samantha: For reporting, can you produce a CSV with per-request latency, model variant, token counts, and a dashboard screenshot? We need a summary that product and execs can read quickly.
[07:20] Carlos: Yes, we'll produce a benchmark report: raw CSV, aggregate stats (P50/P95/P99), throughput/CPU/GPU utilization, token counts, and a short summary PDF with go/no-go callouts. We'll also include all config (model, quantization, batch size).

[09:00] Priya: Quick question on dataset: we'll provide a 500-sample evaluation set for acceptance tests and a larger 10k trace for load shaping. Is that enough?
[09:12] Carlos: That's perfect. We'll use the 500 for quality/regression tests and the 10k for throughput/load shaping. For the soak we'll run multiple concurrent virtual clients to simulate 50 qps.

[11:30] Jordan: For the private deployment, network wise we'll need a VPC peering and a security group that allows only specific IPs. Also KMS key policy for encryption. I'll share our network contact after.
[11:50] Lena: Great. On timelines—propose this plan:
 - Week 1 (Oct 6-12): Prep — gather datasets, test credentials, run initial smoke tests.
 - Week 2 (Oct 13-19): Benchmark runs (2-3 days), collect results, iterate config.
 - Week 3 (Oct 20-26): Quality/regression analysis, final tuning, report delivery.
 - Week 4 (Oct 27-Nov 2): Decision & go/no-go meeting.

[14:05] Priya: That timeline looks good, maybe compress to 3 weeks if all goes well. Our critical path is getting the workload traces and KMS details quickly.

[16:00] Carlos: On benchmarks — we propose exact test parameters: model variant A (fp16), model variant B (int8 quant), batch sizes [1,4,8], max sequence 512, concurrency ramp from 5 to 100 virtual clients to find point of degradation. We'll log KV cache hit rates, token generation time per step, and GPU util.
[16:35] Priya: Quick note — we use prefix caching in our app; ensure that KV cache tests include warm and cold-start scenarios.
[16:50] Carlos: Yes, include both warm and cold KV cases. We'll call it out in the report as "KV cash" in a couple spots in the draft (typo likely in transcribe).

[19:20] Samantha: Go/no-go thresholds recap — so P95 <=300ms AND sustain 50 qps soak AND no more than 5% regression on quality metrics. If we fail latency but meet quality, what's the threshold for conditional go?
[19:40] Lena: We defined soft thresholds: if P95 is between 301-350ms, it's a conditional pass pending optimization plan and cost analysis. If regression >5% that's a fail unless there's a clear mitigation.

[22:00] Priya: Reporting format — raw CSV with columns: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, latency_ms, gpu_util, cpu_util. Plus a single-slide executive summary: pass/fail per acceptance criterion and recommended next steps.
[22:25] Carlos: We'll include that, plus a JSON config file and the scripts used so you can reproduce. We'll upload to the shared drive and provide a link.

[25:00] Jordan: Security — we'll need a formal SOC2 report and shared responsibility doc. Can Redwood provide a SOC2 summary and a short KMS integration guide?
[25:15] Lena: Yes, we'll include SOC2 summary and KMS integration steps in the runbook. For SSO we'll provide SAML metadata.

[28:40] Samantha: Can you also include cost modeling? We need an estimate of expected monthly cost at 100k requests/day after POC.
[28:50] Lena: We'll produce a cost model in the report with assumptions: average tokens per request, batching efficiency, and predicted monthly spend across hosted vs dedicated.

[32:10] Priya: One more technical ask — we need to ensure deterministic prompts for the 500-sample test; we'll provide seeds and expected outputs where applicable.
[32:25] Carlos: Good, we'll run deterministic sampling and compare outputs; drift metric will be percent of outputs that differ beyond the defined thresholds.

[39:00] Lena: To confirm acceptance criteria one more time: P95 <=300ms (hard), P95 301-350ms conditional, sustain 50 qps soak for 30 min, quality regression <=5%, security checklist complete. Reporting: CSV + dashboard + executive slide.

[44:10] Priya: Sounds good, we'll sign off on those criteria once we get the written runbook.

[50:00] Carlos: We'll draft a runbook and the benchmark scripts and send by Oct 9. Expect a link to a shared folder.

[57:30] Lena: Any blockers on your side?
[57:40] Jordan: Just internal approval for KMS sharing, should be ok within 48 hours.
[58:10] Samantha: We'll confirm the 500-sample set today.

[60:00] Lena: Great. Recap of next steps: Lena sends runbook & SOC2 summary; Carlos sends benchmark configs/scripts; Priya sends datasets and SLO doc; Jordan confirms networking/KMS details. We'll schedule the benchmark window for week of Oct 13.
[61:00] Priya: Thanks all, looking forward to seeing results.
[61:10] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.
